title: What If You Had a 3-Meter Chameleon Tongue? 🦎
description:
What if humans had a chameleon's tongue? A chameleon's tongue can stretch over twice its body length and the fastest ones go zero to sixty in about a hundredth of a second, launched off a bone by stretchy collagen sleeves like a slingshot, with spit about 400 times thicker than ours.

Sources:
https://www.brown.edu/news/2016-01-04/chameleon
https://www.nature.com/articles/nphys3795
https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2016/01/160104080020.htm

Animated in the Copperplate Engraving style.

topic: What if humans had a chameleon's tongue?
script:
You'd never miss a snack again
with a chameleon's tongue.
But talking? Ruined.
A chameleon's tongue can stretch
over twice its body length.
For you, that's more than three meters,
bunched up inside your mouth.
And it's fast.
The quickest ones go zero to sixty
in about a hundredth of a second.
The trick is a bone.
The tongue sits on it like a sock on a finger.
A ring of muscle squeezes stretchy collagen sleeves,
loading them like a slingshot.
Then it lets go.
The tongue flies off the bone,
and the sticky tip lands first.
That spit is about four hundred times thicker than yours,
so a bug can't pull free.
You could grab a snack
from across the room
before anyone saw you move.
So what would you snatch first
with a three meter tongue?
key_facts: Chameleon tongues can extend over twice the body length (up to ~2.5x in small species)
Tiny Rhampholeon chameleons' tongues accelerate at about 264 g, 0 to 60 mph in roughly a hundredth of a second (Anderson 2016)
The tongue sits on the entoglossal (hyoid) bone; the accelerator muscle squeezes and loads elastic collagen sheaths that then launch it off the bone like a catapult
Chameleon tongue mucus is about 400 times more viscous than human saliva (Brau et al., Nature Physics 2016)
For a 1.75 m human, twice body length would be about 3.5 m
